related_questions.question: Is Japan safe to visit right now?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, Japan is generally considered safe for tourists. Most travel advisories for Japan, including from the U.S. Department of State and Smartraveller, indicate a Level 1 advisory, which means travelers should exercise normal precautions.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, Japan is generally considered safe for tourists

list.title: Crime:
list.snippet: Japan has low crime rates, making it a relatively safe destination. Petty theft can occur, but violent crime is rare.

list.title: Natural Disasters:
list.snippet: Japan is prone to earthquakes, tsunamis, and volcanic activity. Travelers should be aware of these risks and have a plan in case of an emergency.

list.title: Health:
list.snippet: Vaccinations for measles, Hepatitis A and B, and Japanese encephalitis (for extended stays in rural areas) are recommended.

list.title: Transportation:
list.snippet: Public transportation is generally safe and efficient, but travelers should be aware of crowded conditions during peak hours, especially on the subway.

list.title: Other Considerations:
list.snippet: Be aware of your surroundings, avoid walking alone at night in unfamiliar areas, and be cautious of scams, especially involving money.

text_blocks.snippet: Overall: Japan is a safe country to visit, but travelers should still take basic precautions to ensure a smooth and enjoyable trip.
